Product-Led vs Sales-Led vs Partner-Led Growth

Strategy

In short: Product-led, sales-led and partner-led growth are different organizations, not just different tactics. Choose the primary motion from the product and the buyer, build the organization for it, and add the others in support.

Key points

  • Product-led needs value without a conversation, short time to value, and a price and buyer that can decide alone.
  • Sales-led needs a price high enough to pay for selling, a repeatable process and enough qualified demand; it scales with headcount.
  • Partner-led needs a product that fits a partner's offer and terms that pay them; its risks are slow first revenue and concentration.
  • Many founders decide they are product-led because it is cheaper rather than because it is true.
  • Restricted categories tilt toward partner-led and sales-led motions, which depend less on paid acquisition through large platforms.

Every company acquires customers through some combination of three motions: the product sells itself, people sell it, or other companies sell it. The words for these are product-led, sales-led, and partner-led, and while most companies use more than one, each needs a primary motion, because the three require different organizations.

Product-led

The product is the main acquisition channel. People find it, try it free or cheaply, get value quickly, and pay to get more. Marketing drives sign-ups; the product does the convincing; sales, if it exists, arrives late to expand accounts.

It requires a product that delivers value without a conversation, a short time to that value, a price low enough to decide alone, and a buyer who can decide alone. It breaks when the product needs setup, integration, or trust before it is useful, when the buyer needs approval from others, or when the price is high enough to need a business case.

The economics are attractive: low cost per customer, high volume. The constraint is that it only works for products and buyers that fit, and many founders decide they are product-led because it is cheaper rather than because it is true.

Sales-led

People sell the product. Marketing generates and qualifies leads; sales runs a process from discovery to close; customer success keeps and expands the account. The product may be complex, expensive, or dependent on trust and configuration.

It requires a price high enough to pay for the sales cost, a buyer who expects a conversation, a repeatable process, and enough qualified demand to keep the team busy. It breaks when the price cannot carry the cost of selling, when the founder is the only person who can sell it, or when the pipeline depends on channels that have been closed to the category.

The economics are heavier and more predictable. The constraint is that it scales with headcount, and headcount is slow and expensive.

Partner-led

Other companies distribute the product: platforms that embed it, resellers, agencies, integration partners, affiliates, marketplaces. The company's own marketing and sales are aimed at partners as much as at end customers.

It requires a product that fits inside another company's offer, terms that make the partner money, and the patience to build relationships that take months to produce. It breaks when the partner's incentive is misaligned, when the company depends on one partner, or when the product needs more support than the partner can give.

The economics can be the best of the three once running: low marginal cost per customer, and distribution that no ad platform can revoke. The constraint is time to first revenue, and the risk of concentration in a single partner.

Why a primary motion matters

Each motion needs a different organization. Product-led needs product, data, and growth engineering. Sales-led needs a sales team, enablement, and pipeline marketing. Partner-led needs partnership managers, program terms, and partner marketing. A small company that tries to build all three builds none properly.

Choose the primary motion from the product and buyer, not from preference. Then add the others where they support it: sales to expand product-led accounts, partners to extend a sales-led company's reach, product-led onboarding to reduce a partner-led company's support burden.

For a company the platforms restrict

Restricted categories tilt the choice. Product-led motions that depend on cheap paid acquisition through the large platforms lose their main engine. Partner-led and sales-led motions, which run on relationships, affiliates, and channels that choose to carry the product, are less exposed. That is one reason affiliate and partner programs are often the first thing worth building in these categories.

lowob takeaway: Product-led, sales-led, and partner-led are different organizations, not just different tactics. Choose the primary motion from the product and the buyer, build the organization for it, and add the others in support.

Common questions

What is the difference between product-led, sales-led and partner-led growth?

In product-led growth the product sells itself; in sales-led, people sell it; in partner-led, other companies distribute it. Each requires a different organization.

How do I choose between product-led and sales-led growth?

Choose from the product and buyer, not preference. Product-led breaks when the product needs setup or trust, the buyer needs approval from others, or the price needs a business case.

Can a startup run product-led, sales-led and partner-led at the same time?

Most use more than one, but each needs a primary motion. A small company that tries to build all three builds none properly.

Which growth motion works best when ad platforms restrict your category?

Partner-led and sales-led motions are less exposed, because they run on relationships, affiliates and channels that choose to carry the product. That is one reason affiliate and partner programs are often the first thing worth building.
